title: Otsuka’s JYNARQUE™ (tolvaptan) Approved by U.S. FDA as the First Treatment to Slow Kidney Function Decline in Adults at Risk of Rapidly Progressing Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
text: **Landmark Approval: FDA Greenlights JYNARQUE to Slow Kidney Function Decline in ADPKD Patients**  The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted approval to Otsuka's JYNARQUE (tolvaptan) as the first treatment to slow kidney function decline in adults at risk of rapidly progressing Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD). This groundbreaking approval offers new hope to patients living with ADPKD, a genetic disorder that affects approximately 120,000 Americans. ADPKD is characterized by the growth of numerous cysts on the kidneys, leading to chronic kidney disease and eventual kidney failure. JYNARQUE works by blocking the release of antidiuretic hormone, which helps to slow the growth of cysts and preserve kidney function. With this approval, patients with ADPKD can now have access to a treatment that has been shown to slow disease progression and improve quality of life.

Led by coach Emily Chen, the team applied the principles of Lean to streamline their design and production process. By identifying and eliminating waste, they were able to build a more efficient and effective robot. "We used Lean to create a 'pull' system, where each stage of production only received components when they were needed," explained Chen. STEMpunk's winning robot, aptly named "Efficiency," is a testament to the power of Lean in the world of STEM education.
